chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had a mother who was a slave. When death approached him, a man from our companions went and bought his mother, and stipulated upon her: 'I am buying you and emancipating you, so when your son, so-and-so son of so-and-so, dies and you inherit him, give me half of what you inherit, on the condition that you give me the pledge of Allah and the pledge of His Messenger.' She was pleased with that, so she gave him the pledge of Allah and the pledge of His Messenger to fulfill it for him. The man bought her and emancipated her upon that condition, and her son died after that. So she inherited him, and there was no other heir for him.

He said, so Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He did well by her and will be rewarded for it. This is a jurist (faqih), and the Muslims are upon their conditions, and it is upon her to fulfill for him what she pledged to Allah and His Messenger regarding it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on stipulating inheritance shares when emancipating a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'al-Muslimuna 'ala shurutihim' (Muslims are bound by their conditions) within the context of manumission, where a master buys his slave mother, frees her, and stipulates she pays him half her inheritance from her son. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates this arrangement, emphasizing that the condition is legally binding provided the mother fulfills her pledge to Allah and the Messenger, highlighting the intersection of contract law and familial inheritance in Shia jurisprudence. The narrative underscores the importance of fulfilling religious covenants ('ahd') as a condition for the validity of such financial stipulations.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa and Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had a mother who was a slave. So when the death presented itself to him, a man from our companions and bought his mother, and stipulated a condition upon her, ‘I am buying you and emancipating (liberated) you, so when your son dies, so and so son of so and so, and when you inherit him, so give me half of what you inherit, and the condition that you would be giving that, vowing by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and vowing by His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’. So she was pleased with that, and she gave him the vow of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> to convince him. So the man bought her and emancipated (liberated) her upon that condition, and her son died after that. So she inherited him and there did not happen to be any inheritor apart from her.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He did a favour to her, and he should be recompensed by her. This is for a Faqih and the Muslims during the stipulations of their conditions, and it is upon her that she should fulfill whatever she had vowed by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, to him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all ibn Mahbub from al-‘ Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim Muhammad who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who had a mother who was owned by someone. When it was the time of his death a certain person of our people went and bought his mother. He set the condition that he buys her and sets her free; if after the death of her son so and so, son of so and so, when she will inherit his legacy, she must pay him one-half of what she will inherit. She must promise before Allah and the Messenger of Allah to fulfil this agreement. She agreed and promised before Allah and the Messenger of Allah to act according to the agreement. The man bought and freed her according to the condition and her son died thereafter. She inherited him because there was no other heir except her.

Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He has done a favor to her and has his rewards for it. He is a scholar of fiqh (Islamic laws) and Muslims stand by their conditions. She must complete the agreement about which she has promised before Allah and His messenger.”’
